title: Metallic specular blob implausibly bright in ReflectionProbe when light size >0.0 in Forward+
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: v4.7.1.rc1.official [17e2686e0], v4.7.stable.arch_linux [5b4e0cb0f], v4.5.2.stable.official [6ce3de25a], v4.0.4.stable.official [fc0b241c9] ### System information Godot v4.7.1.rc1 - CachyOS Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Mon, 29 Jun 2026 14:34:33 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti (nvidia; 610.43.02) - AMD Ryzen 5 3600X 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 15.52 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description The specular blob on metallic materials captured by ReflectionProbe emitted from lights with size >0.0 creates absolutely hideous reflections that add implausible amounts of light to the scene and make diffuse surfaces look glossy. The problem becomes noticeably problematic when the metallic material's roughness is set <0.1. ### Light size set to 0.1m Specular blob captured by ReflectionProbe is adding excessive light to the scene. The lights have default energy of 1.0. ### Light size set to 0.0m (default) Specular blob captured by ReflectionProbe is contributing expected amount of light to the scene. The lights have default energy of 1.0. ## . The problem is exacerbated especially by increasing the reflection roughness layers. By reducing the roughness layers from the default of 8 to 4, the problem is slightly less bad: But this obviously causes the other issues you would expect from limiting roughness layers, such as overly glossy reflections. ReflectionProbe update mode always and update mode once have slightly different presentation of this issue. The issue is also not always visible with update mode once, presumably because of the sparser sampling, while the issue is always visible with update mode always. The issue does not seem to be present on compatibility. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Add a reflection probe to a scene 2. Add a mesh with a metallicity of 1.0 and a roughness < 0.1 to within the bounds of the reflection prob 3. Add a light to where the reflection probe can see the metallic mesh's specular blob 4. Set the lights size to 0.05 ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [metal-specular.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29666383/metal-specular.zip)
